fieldissues.issue: “Authoritarianism,” “Government Power Abuse,” executive-overreach, and power-centralization labels do not describe the administration’s decision to stay outside an international COVID-19 response and vaccine effort.
The tags do not name the WHO initiative, vaccine development, or the U.S. decision and repeat broad political labels.

proposedchanges.change: Use a foreign-policy or global-health category if available, with no abuse-of-power subcategory. Replace the generic labels with “WHO initiative,” “COVID-19 vaccine development,” “U.S. nonparticipation,” and “international pandemic response.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long describe the proposed $8 billion WHO-led initiative, the administration’s refusal, and the distinction between proposed funding and spent funds. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-2919. The title and descriptions are distinct and do not claim that refusal proved the United States lost access to a vaccine.

fieldissues.issue: The preserved long description states that Trump joined a racketeering enterprise, violated federal law, collaborated with violent crime families, and benefited from criminal intimidation. The supplied medium says the reports document attributed allegations and scrutiny and that no criminal charges resulted.
“Organized Crime Collaboration and Racketeering Enterprise” presents the allegations as established, contrary to the supplied medium’s qualification.

proposedchanges.change: Resolve the conflicting descriptions before release. Rewrite the long field to attribute each land, construction, and organized-crime claim to the cited reporting or records, and remove conclusions that Trump participated in racketeering or violated RICO unless a finding supports them.

Use an allegation-focused label for reported business ties and investigation. Remove “racketeering enterprise” and “criminal enterprise participation” as established facts unless supported by a legal finding.

evidencebasis: The supplied medium says the reports discuss alleged organized-crime ties and records, note questioning in investigations, and report no criminal charges. The long field converts these allegations into conclusions. Politico and CNN URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-293. The medium supplies the necessary qualification; the preserved long and metadata need source-aligned review.

fieldissues.issue: “Authoritarianism,” “Government Power Abuse,” executive overreach, and power centralization do not describe a proposed Parler stake tied to a presidential candidate’s use of the platform.
The tags do not identify the proposed ownership arrangement or ethics concern.

proposedchanges.change: Use a conflicts-of-interest or financial-benefit category if available. Replace the generic labels with “Parler,” “Trump Organization,” “40 percent stake offer,” “campaign communications,” and “ethics concerns.” Keep the distinction between a proposed stake and an accepted benefit.

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long describe the proposed 40 percent stake and say officials stopped discussions over ethics concerns; neither says Trump accepted the stake or joined Parler. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-2940. The long description distinguishes the proposal from a completed transaction or ethics violation.

fieldissues.issue: “FBI recruits” states as fact what the supplied medium and long attribute to Biggs’s defense lawyer and say lacks independent evidence or FBI confirmation.
“Transparency Obstruction” and “FBI informants” can imply a confirmed informant relationship, while the account says that relationship is unverified.

proposedchanges.change: Until the source basis is resolved, use an attributed title such as: “Biggs’s lawyer says he provided FBI information about anti-fascists.”
Remove “FBI informants” as a confirmed label. Use “Joseph Biggs,” “defense lawyer’s claim,” “FBI contact allegation,” and “Proud Boys events,” and keep the relationship attributed.

evidencebasis: The supplied long description says the informant account comes from Biggs’s lawyer, has no FBI confirmation or independent evidence, and gives an unclear event date. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-2951. The title and metadata need the same attribution already present in the medium and long.

Add “White House” and “Fox News” if publisher and administration organizations are included in this tag field.

fieldissues.issue: “National Security Violations,” “War / Militarization,” Iran, and military-escalation tags do not describe Scaramucci’s 2020 endorsement of Joe Biden and criticism of Trump.

proposedchanges.change: Use an election or political-campaign category if available. Replace the war labels with “2020 presidential campaign,” “Biden endorsement,” “former Trump official,” and “political dissent.”

notes: Existing entry-2973. The medium and long are distinct and appropriately limit the claim to Scaramucci’s statement.

fieldissues.issue: “Gives terrorist treatment” is a metaphor that can imply the ICC was formally designated or treated as a terrorist organization; the described action was sanctions on two officials.
“War / Militarization,” Iran, and military-escalation tags do not identify the ICC sanctions and the Afghanistan investigation.
The list is empty although the ICC and Human Rights Watch are named in the supplied account.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Trump administration sanctions ICC officials during Afghanistan war-crimes inquiry.”
Replace the Iran-war labels with “International Criminal Court,” “Afghanistan inquiry,” “U.S. sanctions,” “Fatou Bensouda,” and “Phakiso Mochochoko.”
Add “International Criminal Court” and “Human Rights Watch.”

evidencebasis: The supplied long description identifies the two sanctioned officials, the Afghanistan investigation, Pompeo’s stated rationale, and Human Rights Watch’s criticism. It says sanctions did not determine guilt or establish the effect on the inquiry. The Trump File URL is retained.
notes: Existing entry-2984. Keep the sanctions’ stated rationale and the unresolved allegations separate.

fieldissues.issue: “Begins authoritarian attacks on the military” is a broad characterization; the medium and long describe specific remarks accusing Pentagon leaders of favoring wars for contractor interests.
“Iran conflict” and “military escalation” do not name the remarks about Pentagon leaders, defense contractors, and deployments.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Trump accuses Pentagon leaders of backing wars to benefit contractors.”
Replace “Iran conflict” and “military escalation” with “Pentagon leadership,” “defense contractors,” “U.S. deployments,” and “military remarks.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long describe Trump’s statements, his denial of the “losers” and “suckers” report, and prior tensions over deployments. They do not report an institutional action against the military. All four URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-2995. The category broadly fits the military subject; the title and tags should name the specific remarks.

fieldissues.issue: “Scams supporters” asserts deceptive intent. The medium and long describe recurring donations preselected by default and say not every recurring contribution was unauthorized.
“Authoritarianism,” “Government Power Abuse,” and executive-overreach labels do not describe the campaign’s online fundraising design.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Trump campaign preselects recurring donations on fundraising pages.”

Use the existing “Grift / Financial Exploitation” category if it covers fundraising practices, with a campaign-donation subcategory if available. Replace executive-power labels with “recurring donations,” “WinRed,” “donor opt-out,” and “campaign refunds.”

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long describe the default weekly selection, opt-out burden, and reported refunds, while saying the record does not establish every recurring gift was unauthorized. Both URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-3004. The title should describe the design without asserting intent or unauthorized charges for all donors.

fieldissues.issue: “donald trump,” “election interference,” and “democratic institution undermining” repeat the person and category rather than identifying the exchange’s subjects.

The title and description quote the ballot remark, but the long description adds broader interpretation about how rhetoric framed lawful counting; this reading should remain clearly distinct from the documented exchange.

proposedchanges.change: Replace duplicated category and person labels with “peaceful transfer of power,” “ballot counting,” “2020 election,” and “election result acceptance.”
Keep the interpretation explicitly framed as context or analysis, separate from the exact quote and documented refusal to promise a peaceful transfer.

evidencebasis: The supplied medium and long identify the September 23 exchange and state that Trump did not commit to a peaceful transfer. They also say the remark alone did not cause officials to discard ballots or establish later actions. Both URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-3015. The title, medium, and long are distinct; the issue is tag duplication and clear separation of fact from interpretation.
